inserts.title: Prolactin feeding depends on brood experience
paragraphs: Lehrman's prolactin protocol delivered 450 international units over 7 days, after which a squab was presented to each bird. The design compared treated birds with controls and grouped the birds by whether they had reared young before. Each parent's feeding was recorded against its own history. The hormone sequence and the feeding test were carried out in the same birds.

Experienced parents usually began feeding once prolactin had been given. Inexperienced birds failed to feed under the same sequence, although they responded physiologically to the hormone. The behavioral outcome therefore depended on the bird's history as well as the hormone. The experienced parents and the inexperienced birds were both tested with the same squab.

The crop's proliferating epithelium is the tissue that supplies milk, and it responds in the periphery. A physiological change in the crop therefore accompanies the hormone treatment, while the feeding decision depends on the bird's experience. The crop tissue therefore identifies the physiology that the behavioral test follows.
notes: Prolactin feeding depends on brood experience.

Lehrman's prolactin protocol delivered 450 international units over 7 days, after which a squab was presented to each bird

The design compared treated birds with controls and grouped the birds by whether they had reared young before. Each parent's feeding was recorded against its own history. The hormone sequence and the feeding test were carried out in the same birds.

Inexperienced birds failed to feed under the same sequence, although they responded physiologically to the hormone. The behavioral outcome therefore depended on the bird's history as well as the hormone. The experienced parents and the inexperienced birds were both tested with the same squab.

inserts.title: Female nest-cooing marks the nesting phase
paragraphs: Female nest-cooing is a vocal display given at the nest site. Females join males in this display and may continue alone after the male leaves to gather material. Daily observations separated these vocalizations from bow-cooing and from physical construction. The pairs were recorded through the egg period, so the vocal record covers the whole reproductive stage.

Cheng described an abrupt end to female cooing after the second egg. That change marks the transition from nest building toward incubation, so the vocal record tracks the reproductive stage of the pair. The end of female cooing marks a clear behavioral boundary in the pair's reproductive timeline.

Records of when cooing happens establish the timing of the signal. Playback and hormone manipulations then test the physiological and social effects of cooing within the same pairs. The records therefore link the vocal phase to the stage of the pair's nest.
notes: Female nest-cooing marks the nesting phase.

inserts.title: Estrogen and progesterone restore nest building
paragraphs: Cheng and Silver used reproductively experienced females after ovariectomy to reduce endogenous ovarian hormone input. They compared estradiol benzoate, progesterone, both steroids in a timed regimen, and sesame oil, with untreated males as partners. The regimen was designed so that the estrogen phase comes first, which the timing of the doses shows.

Estradiol benzoate was given on courtship days 4–10, and progesterone was added on days 8 and 10 in the combined condition. The doses were 50 micrograms of estradiol benzoate and 100 micrograms of progesterone, timed to follow estrogen exposure. The progesterone doses on days 8 and 10 were given after estrogen exposure had begun.

The combined regimen produced the strongest nest-building response. Its timing shows that the order of the two signals matters for construction, and the schedule defines that order. The combined schedule, rather than either steroid alone, produced the full nest-building response.
notes: Estrogen and progesterone restore nest building.

inserts.title: Construction requires more than picking up material
paragraphs: Cheng and Silver separated picking up and dropping nest material, carrying it to a site, and tucking it into the nest bowl. These measures distinguish interaction with an available object from the coordinated construction needed for a functional nest. Each action is scored separately, so the tucking and carrying measures can be compared across the same pairs.

Females given the combined regimen more reliably performed the later construction actions than females given either hormone alone or oil. Records of untreated males allowed each partner's contribution to be measured separately. The later construction actions were most reliable in the combined-regimen females.

On days 8 and 10, pairs lacking completed nests received an experimenter-built nest. Tucking material into that nest therefore involved rearranging an existing structure rather than constructing a new one. Pairs without a completed nest were provided with one, which made the tucking measure reflect rearrangement.
notes: Construction requires more than picking up material.

inserts.title: Acoustic feedback restores follicular growth
paragraphs: Cheng recorded female nest-coos before muting and played those calls back during pairing. Auditory input was restored while normal vocal sound production stayed impaired, which isolates hearing from vocal output. The muting procedure is reversible, so the same females can be tested under different playback conditions.

The diameter of the same dominant ovarian follicle was measured before and after the playback period. The initial diameters were 4–5 millimeters across treatment conditions, so each change is measured from a common starting point. The follicle diameters were compared between the own-call, male-call and no-playback groups.

Own-call playback produced substantially more growth than male-call playback. The rescue supports an auditory contribution from the female's own display, and the neural circuit carrying that signal is the link still to be identified. Own-call playback produced the largest growth in the muted females.
notes: Acoustic feedback restores follicular growth.

Cheng recorded female nest-coos before muting and played those calls back during pairing

inserts.title: Hearing and bodily feedback are distinct inputs
paragraphs: Cheng distinguished hearing a nest-coo from proprioceptive feedback, which is sensory information from performing the movements of a vocal display. Playback restored the auditory stimulus while the muted females' sound production stayed impaired. Proprioceptive feedback comes from the movements that produce the call, not from the sound it makes.

Playback can also provoke attempted vocal movements and their bodily signals. Auditory rescue therefore engages one route, and the motor and sensory consequences of calling form a separate route. Playback restored the sound the female heard, so the auditory route was tested alone.

Courtship promotes female behavior, and that behavior stimulates the female herself. This reciprocal link makes the reproductive sequence a loop, with follicular growth as the measured endpoint. Reproductive growth in the females therefore depends on both auditory and bodily signals.
notes: Hearing and bodily feedback are distinct inputs.

inserts.title: Hormones promote nest activity while copulation stays rare
paragraphs: Liley's estrogen and combined estrogen–progesterone treatments supported female soliciting and nest-building activity. Nest-oriented activity was greatest under long days, while begging and sexual crouching stayed infrequent in the hormone-treated birds. The estrogen and combined treatments both promoted nest-directed activity under long days.

The treatment lasted 15 days and was combined with daily access to an active male. Each reproductive action was recorded separately, so the results describe specific behaviors rather than a single judgment of breeding condition. Each action category was counted, so begging and crouching are reported on their own.

Hormonal facilitation is behavior-specific. A treatment can promote nest-directed activity while the full sequence of mating and egg laying remains infrequent, and this pattern was observed in intact females. Hormone treatment shapes which reproductive actions the female performs in an intact context.
notes: Hormones promote nest activity while copulation stays rare.

inserts.title: Volume changes call for cellular measures
paragraphs: Neural plasticity is a change in nervous-system structure or function with state or experience. Nottebohm's measurements established seasonal variation in song-nucleus volume, and that volume combines neurons, their processes and other tissue components. The canary volume measures were taken from adult birds in different seasons.

A seasonal increase can reflect cell size, cell density or cell number. Histology distinguishes these measures, and recordings or behavioral assays address the consequences for vocal output. The sparrow measures add the cellular basis for these volume differences.

Tramontin and colleagues measured these cellular attributes in white-crowned sparrows exposed to controlled breeding-like conditions. Their results supply the cellular detail that the canary volume data lacked. Together the two studies place seasonal growth in the cellular changes of the song system.
notes: Volume changes call for cellular measures.

Neural plasticity is a change in nervous-system structure or function with state or experience

inserts.title: HVC expands before its targets
paragraphs: Tramontin and colleagues measured the volume of HVC, RA and Area X after the combined long-day and testosterone intervention. HVC reached about 94 percent of its eventual breeding-like size within 7 days, while its targets grew more slowly. The treatment combined long days with testosterone, and each nucleus was measured at the same two time points.

RA and Area X reached their larger condition at the 20-day measurement, after HVC had already expanded. The order of these changes is the first evidence for a sequence of anatomical responses. HVC volume is already close to its final value at 7 days, while RA and Area X are still growing.

The nuclei were measured across one defined time course, so the order of growth is a result of the treatment. Manipulating HVC or its projections would test whether this transsynaptic sequence operates. The ordering of these responses is consistent with a sequence running from HVC to its targets.
notes: HVC expands before its targets.

inserts.title: RA grows through larger tissue volume
paragraphs: RA grew more slowly than HVC after breeding-like stimulation. Its neurons enlarged early, and the later increase in nucleus volume came with a drop in neuron density rather than a rise in total neuron number. RA's soma enlargement appears early, and its volume increase comes later in the same birds.

By day 20, the same general neuronal population occupied a larger volume of tissue. HVC differed, because substantial population growth contributed to its enlargement within the first 7 days. The density decrease in RA contrasts with the density stability seen in HVC.

A lower density fits more space taken up by neuronal processes or other tissue components. The result identifies different cellular signatures of seasonal growth in two connected song nuclei. Each nucleus therefore carries its own cellular signature of seasonal growth.
notes: RA grows through larger tissue volume.

inserts.title: Song duration and consistency are separate measures
paragraphs: A spectrogram displays sound frequency over time, so individual song components can be measured. Tramontin and colleagues divided the white-crowned sparrow song into whistle, warble and buzz portions, using the published 2 kHz and 0.5 s calibration bars. The whistle, warble and buzz portions were measured from the same published song spectrograms.

Mean song duration was 1.80 seconds after 7 days of breeding-like stimulation and 1.84 seconds after 20 days. Whistle duration stayed close to 0.51 and 0.52 seconds across the two time points. The duration of each portion was stable across the two time points.

Average duration and repeat-to-repeat consistency describe different properties of the vocal pattern. The average gives the central timing, while variation across repeated songs gives the consistency. Consistency across repeated songs is measured separately from the average timing.
notes: Song duration and consistency are separate measures.

A spectrogram displays sound frequency over time, so individual song components can be measured

inserts.title: Oxytocin accelerates pup retrieval in females
paragraphs: Marlin and colleagues tested oxytocin's central behavioral effects in female mice, a mammalian system that clarifies how the hormone acts. Oxytocin is a neuropeptide made by hypothalamic neurons, including those in the paraventricular nucleus, or PVN. The retrieval measure captures how quickly the female returns the pup, which is a learned response.

Initially inexperienced virgin females were housed with a mother and her pups. Systemic oxytocin, or optical stimulation of PVN oxytocin neurons, sped retrieval of isolated pups, and many females began within 12 hours of co-housing. The oxytocin manipulation changed the speed at which social experience produced retrieval.

Saline-treated females needed longer experience before retrieving. Oxytocin therefore changed how quickly a social setting produced the response, which makes it a regulator of when experience becomes behavior. The PVN supplies the oxytocin-producing neurons whose optical stimulation produced the same speeding.
notes: Oxytocin accelerates pup retrieval in females.

Marlin and colleagues tested oxytocin's central behavioral effects in female mice, a mammalian system that clarifies how the hormone acts

Explanation 2.

inserts.title: Oxytocin receptors sit on inhibitory interneurons
paragraphs: Interneurons are local neurons that influence neighboring cells within a circuit. Marlin and colleagues identified oxytocin receptors on inhibitory cortical interneurons marked by parvalbumin or somatostatin. The labeled interneurons were identified by their parvalbumin or somatostatin content.

About 30–40 percent of the labeled parvalbumin-positive and somatostatin-positive populations expressed oxytocin receptors. Hormone sensitivity therefore reached cells positioned to regulate local inhibition, not only excitatory output neurons. The receptor-positive fraction of each population was measured in the same cortex.

Oxytocin's effect on inhibition is a candidate route to control of local circuits. Synaptic recordings show how inhibition changed during hormone exposure and learning-related stimulation. The overlap places hormone sensitivity in the inhibitory interneurons of the auditory cortex.
notes: Oxytocin receptors sit on inhibitory interneurons.

inserts.title: Oxytocin acts most strongly on acquisition
paragraphs: Local oxytocin delivery to the left auditory cortex accelerated retrieval in inexperienced females. Optical stimulation of oxytocin axons in the same region produced a similar acceleration, which links a localized input to acquisition. The left-cortex oxytocin delivery and the optical axon stimulation used the same target region.

Oxytocin-receptor antagonists infused into the left cortex left retrieval largely intact once the behavior was established. An antagonist blocks receptor activation, so it tests ongoing signaling apart from earlier exposure. Antagonist infusion after learning showed that the performance of the behavior persists.

Acquisition and performance therefore have different experimental dependencies. The result fits lasting circuit changes after oxytocin-assisted experience, which the established behavior shows when receptor signaling is blocked. Acquisition and performance therefore have distinct dependencies on oxytocin signaling.
notes: Oxytocin acts most strongly on acquisition.

2: Ring doves are domesticated columbids in which both parents incubate eggs and feed their young. Lehrman described a clutch of two eggs, about 14 days of incubation, and parental regurgitation of crop contents into the squab, the newly hatched young bird. Lehrman's ring-dove experiments tested whether this parental feeding depended on the hormones and experience that prepare the adult for it.

The **crop** is a bilobed expansion of the esophagus. Its epithelial lining proliferates during incubation and supplies the cellular material called crop milk. Pigeon dissections distinguish a thin non-lactating wall from enlarged, milk-producing lateral lobes. Pigeon crop epithelium therefore serves as a measurable, peripheral marker of the milk-producing state.

Milk-producing tissue supplies nourishment for the young, and its growth is part of the parental program that begins during incubation. The crop therefore links a hormone-driven tissue change to the feeding behavior that follows. Feeding behavior and crop physiology are both measured, so the link between tissue and behavior can be examined directly.
3: **Prolactin** is a pituitary hormone that promotes crop development in columbids. Lehrman administered 450 international units over 7 days and then presented a squab, comparing hormonally treated birds with controls and separating birds by their reproductive history. The hormone was given in a fixed sequence, so the timing of the squab presentation followed the same schedule in every bird.

Previously experienced parents generally began feeding after prolactin treatment. Birds without prior brood experience failed to feed under the same artificial sequence, even though they responded physiologically to the treatment. Prior experience changed the behavioral consequence of the hormone. The contrast between experienced and inexperienced birds shows that the same hormone dose produced different behavior.

Pigeon histology identifies proliferating crop epithelium, the peripheral tissue that supplies milk. This tissue response is measured in the periphery, so the crop provides a visible sign of the hormonal change that accompanies feeding. Histology shows the proliferating epithelium that accompanies the milk-producing state in the same tissue.
4: Lehrman reduced sensation near the crop by applying 0.5 cubic centimeters of the local anesthetic Efocaine 2 days before a squab was presented. A comparison group received the anesthetic elsewhere on the body, which controlled for the effects of the drug itself. The anesthetic was delivered at a fixed interval before the squab presentation, so the timing of the block was controlled.

Local treatment near the crop reduced parental feeding. **Peripheral feedback** is sensory information returning from the body to the nervous system, and crop distension and contact with a squab are candidate sources of that information. Crop distension and direct contact both give the bird sensory information from the crop during feeding.

The location of the anesthetic determined the behavioral outcome, which points to a sensory contribution from the crop. The crop tissue shown here comes from pigeons, while the feeding experiments used ring doves. The anesthetic effect was therefore tied to the location of the block, which points to the crop as the source of the signal.
5: Ring-dove nest building involves a division of labor: males usually gather and transport material, while females remain at the nest site and tuck material into the developing nest. Martinez-Vargas and Erickson recorded these actions separately during the days before the first egg. Males gathered and carried material, and females placed it, so each partner's share of the work was recorded separately.

Established pairs received space, nest sites and alternative materials. Repeated observations related the male's gathering to the female's attendance and construction, rather than treating total nest size as the only behavioral measure. Each pair received the same nest materials, so differences in gathering reflect the birds rather than the supply.

Male transport increased when females were established at the nest, so each partner's activity responded to the other. Coordinated behavior can arise through signals exchanged between the birds during the nesting period. The transport response to female attendance shows that male behavior tracks the activity of the female at the nest.
6: **Bow-cooing** is a male courtship vocalization accompanied by a bowing display. Martinez-Vargas and Erickson recorded its frequency across days aligned to the first egg, which allowed a comparison with nest-material transport and female nest attendance in the same reproductive period. Bow-cooing and bowing were recorded together, so the vocal and postural elements of the display were measured as one unit.

Bow-cooing declined as nesting progressed, while material gathering followed a different time course. The behavioral components changed together within the breeding cycle, but they did not share one trajectory or one function. Each component followed its own time course relative to the first egg, which the daily records resolved.

Aligning the records to egg laying provides a common reference event for the observable actions. The temporal pattern shows how the components are arranged across the cycle, which is the basis for testing their links with hormones. The shared reference to egg laying allows the pattern of each behavior to be traced across the same reproductive cycle.
7: **Nest-cooing** is a vocal display given at the nest site. Females join males in this behavior and may continue alone after the male leaves to gather material. Daily observation distinguished female cooing from male bow-cooing and from physical nest construction. Nest-cooing is a display that both sexes produce, so the same vocal behavior can be compared across partners.

Martinez-Vargas and Erickson distinguished nest attendance from active nest soliciting. Cheng described an abrupt cessation of female cooing after the second egg, which linked the vocal phase to the transition toward incubation. Cheng's observation links the end of female cooing to the second egg, which marks the start of incubation.

A vocalization can influence a partner and also return sensory feedback to the bird that produces it. The records establish when cooing occurs, and playback or hormone manipulations are the means of testing its physiological and social effects. Vocal feedback to the female is therefore one candidate route by which the call shapes her reproductive state.
8: Martinez-Vargas and Erickson compared females treated with estrogen and progesterone against oil-treated females before pairing them with males. Hormone replacement supplies an experimental endocrine signal, and the oil group controls for the injection and the vehicle that carries the hormones. The estrogen and progesterone treatment was given to the female before she was paired with a male, so the male met a treated partner.

On the first pairing day, treated females performed more nest soliciting, including wing-flipping and nest-cooing. Their untreated male partners also changed how they gathered material, and female nest attendance was closely associated with male transport. Treated females produced more of these displays on the first day, and the untreated males responded with more transport.

The female alone received the experimental hormones, so a change in male behavior reflects altered signals from his partner. Direct action of the hormones on the male is therefore a different route from the one this experiment tested. Partner signals are therefore a route by which a hormone given to one bird can alter the other bird's nest building.
9: Cheng and Silver used reproductively experienced females after ovariectomy, the surgical removal of the ovaries, to reduce endogenous ovarian hormone contributions. They compared estradiol benzoate, progesterone, both steroids in a timed regimen, and sesame oil, with untreated males as partners.
